title: Serological Pipettes & Pipette-Aid (Pipettor)

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: Used for measuring and transferring larger liquid volumes (typically 1-50 mL) than a micropipette handles, common for bulk media, buffer, and cell culture liquid handling; the graduated pipette is powered by a separate hand-held pipette-aid rather than mouth pipetting.
operatingPrinciple: A graduated glass or plastic pipette is inserted into a motorized or bulb-style pipette-aid (pipettor), which draws liquid up into the pipette by controlled suction/vacuum and dispenses it by controlled release, reading the desired volume off the pipette's printed graduations.
basicOperation: Select a pipette sized appropriately for the volume being measured (using the smallest pipette that comfortably covers the range improves accuracy).
Attach the pipette securely to the pipette-aid.
Draw liquid to slightly above the desired graduation mark, then carefully release to the exact mark, reading at eye level to avoid parallax error.
Dispense against the container wall (or per the specific protocol's technique) at a controlled rate, and use a fresh sterile pipette for each new/different sample to avoid cross-contamination.
importantSettings: Pipette volume/graduation selection matched to the task
maintenance: Keep the pipette-aid's filter (where present) clean and replace it if liquid has been drawn into it.
Store pipette-aids charged (for motorized units) and per manufacturer instructions.

commonErrors.cause: Parallax error when reading the meniscus, or using an oversized pipette for a small volume
commonErrors.fix: Read the graduation at eye level and select a pipette whose range better matches the target volume

commonErrors.problem: Liquid drawn into the pipette-aid itself
commonErrors.cause: Over-drawing past the pipette's capacity, or a failed/missing filter
commonErrors.fix: Never draw past the pipette's top graduation and ensure an intact filter is in place if the unit uses one

safety: Never mouth-pipette — always use a mechanical pipette-aid.
Use a fresh sterile pipette for each different sample or reagent to prevent cross-contamination.
Dispose of used pipettes per the facility's sharps/biohazard waste procedures where applicable.
